title: How PEZ Works
summary: Josh Clark and guest producer Noel (with Chuck Bryant) explore PEZ candy and its dispensers. They cover the candy's basics and manufacturing figures, the 2011 royal wedding PEZ dispensers and high auction prices, eBay's link to PEZ collecting, and the history: Edward Haas III's anti-smoking peppermint mints (the name from the German word for peppermint, "Pfefferminz"), Oscar Uxa's lighter-style dispenser, the shift to fruit flavors and toy dispensers with cartoon heads, and the Pez Girls. They discuss collectibles and licensing (Star Wars, Hello Kitty, Santa, Bicentennial figures, the 2006 Orange County Chopper dispensers), the Pez museum in Burlingame, California, and Pez president Scott McWinney's clash with dispenser smuggler Steve Glew, the "Pez Outlaw," as reported in Playboy. The episode closes with a listener mail about college and student loans from animator Margie.

segments.title: Opening banter about eating PEZ
segments.summary: Josh and Chuck (with guest producer Noel) joke about how they eat PEZ candy, the orange flavor, and the candy's brick shape, and mention a past Los Angeles podcast with candy.

segments.title: PEZ manufacturing facts
segments.summary: The hosts cite PEZ's sugar use (about 50,000 pounds every four days), the roughly 3,000 pounds of pressure used to compress the candy, twelve million tablets a day at the Orange, Connecticut plant, and three billion bricks consumed in the US each year.

segments.title: Candy factory tours and whiskey distillery tours
segments.summary: Chuck and Josh talk about candy factory tours and sampling, then compare them to whiskey distillery tours and the angel's share evaporation.

segments.title: Royal wedding PEZ dispensers and record prices
segments.summary: The hosts describe PEZ dispensers made for the 2011 wedding of William and Kate, which sold for $360 at a charity auction. They also mention a $32,000 astronaut-themed dispenser sold on eBay in 2006.

segments.title: eBay origins and PEZ collecting boom
segments.summary: The hosts say eBay founder Pierre Omidyar was inspired by his partner's PEZ collecting. They note collecting took off in the late 1980s, and recall a Seinfeld episode featuring a Tweety Bird dispenser.

segments.title: Circus barker vs. ringmaster banter
segments.summary: A short tangent in which the hosts joke about whether they would be a circus barker or a ringmaster.

segments.title: Edward Haas III and the origin of PEZ mints
segments.summary: Austrian candy maker Edward Haas III, a germophobe who was also anti-smoking, made peppermint mints to help people quit smoking or freshen breath. The name PEZ comes from an abbreviation of the German word for peppermint. The mints were first sold in tins and wrapped in small candy bars.

segments.title: Oscar Uxa and the lighter-style dispenser
segments.summary: Haas's employee Oscar Uxa designed a dispenser shaped like a cigarette lighter that spit out one mint at a time, replacing hand-to-tin contact. The hosts discuss how the design mimicked smoking and was marketed to kids and adults in Europe and then the US.

segments.title: Pez Girls, candy cigarettes, and gum
segments.summary: The hosts describe the Pez Girls bellhop-style ads that ran from the 1940s to the early 1980s, and then discuss candy cigarettes, gum cigarettes, Big League Chew, and a Rambo-themed gum.

segments.title: Fruit flavors, cartoon heads, and the toy switch
segments.summary: Kids preferred fruit flavors, so PEZ added fruit flavors and sodas, and some flavors were released only outside the US. PEZ then moved to toy dispensers with cartoon heads to make the product more parent-friendly and collectible. The hosts also discuss the sugar stick and Captain Crunch cereal.

segments.title: Collecting, licensing, and PEZ museum
segments.summary: Edward Haas's company grew after his departure, with manufacturing moved abroad while candy stayed in Orange, Connecticut. Dispensers gained feet in 1979 for display. The hosts cover licensing deals, Santa and bicentennial figures, the 2006 Orange County Chopper dispensers, and the Burlingame, California museum.

segments.title: Pez Outlaw Steve Glew and the Playboy article
segments.summary: The hosts discuss Steve Glew, known as the Pez Outlaw, who smuggled and resold rare dispensers from Eastern Europe. They say his business failed after he overextended, and PEZ president Scott McWinney released cheaper counterfeit-style versions. The story was reported in Playboy.

segments.title: Listener mail on college and student loans
segments.summary: Animator Margie writes that the show's remark that college is not required for some jobs struck a chord, and she describes her student loan debt. The hosts agree and suggest a future episode.
